gaps.note: A procedure scheme for how the age composition of a return was derived, each member a sosa:Procedure so that the column can be bound with sosa:usedProcedure. PSC's Fraser sockeye data hold eleven values: Sp. Gr., Comb, Manual, Prnt. Stk., Forecast and Zero; a value for scales from in-season catches with unlikely ages and biased gear types removed; and four compound values, each recorded for one production group, that pair two methods, each labelled with what this card reads as a part of that group, namely Sp. Gr. (Pitt), Manual (Alou); Sp. Gr. (HFly), Comb (Mtch); Sp. Gr. (HFly), Manual (Mtch); and Comb (E. Chil), Sp. Gr. (Chil). PSC's documentation defines four methods: spawning-ground samples; spawning-ground and fishery samples combined; expert judgement informed by similar stocks and by forecast and brood-year age compositions; and the age composition of the parental stock. The other values need PSC's definitions before a term can be written, and the compound values need decomposing in the data or a concept for each combination. No age-composition method exists in smn 0.0.3 or gcdfo 0.0.9: smn's method scheme holds enumeration and fish-length methods, and gcdfo's estimate-method scheme estimates abundance from enumeration data. The methods are PSC's Fraser sockeye practice, so the PSC controlled vocabulary is the natural home; it was not consulted.
gaps.title: How a return's age composition was derived

gaps.note: A general concept for an event that obstructs the upstream migration of adult salmon, such as a landslide or rockfall into a river channel, and a relation from a return, or the fish of a stock in a return year, to such an event, so that data can say a return was exposed to one. DFO's 2025 advice scores the mortality risk from geomorphic events such as landslides separately from temperature and flow risks, which is the use the concept would serve. ENVO_01000692, landslide process, names the geological process and is a candidate related external term; it says nothing about fish passage. gcdfo:InRiverMortalityRate is the rate such an event can raise, not the event. Obstruction events affect salmon of every agency, so the concept belongs in the shared layer.
gaps.title: The Big Bar landslide and the returns it affected

gaps.conflicts: PATO models a particular shape as a determinate subclass of the shape quality (PATO:0002400 fusiform under spindle-shaped, under shape), which supports keeping smn:fusiform as a subclass (Form B). smn's CONVENTIONS section 3 puts code values and categories in SKOS, and the 2026-08-13 migration of six method classes to SKOS concepts is the precedent for re-typing it as a value (Form A). Until one is chosen, the existing class is not shown to be at the wrong level.
gaps.evidence_needed: Brett's ruling on Form A or Form B for smn:fusiform, or a general smn rule on how the values of a characteristic are modelled that also covers shapes.
gaps.note: smn:fusiform is an owl:Class under smn:BodyShape and the only member of its value set: a value of body shape modelled as a kind of the characteristic. That reads correctly only under a determinable and determinate reading, which PATO uses for shapes (PATO:0002400 fusiform under spindle-shaped, under shape). Where characteristic class IRIs are used as observed-property values, fusiform would instead be a result value, which points to a SKOS value scheme. Resolving this means either keeping the subclass and declaring the PATO reading, for example with Tier-3 links to PATO:0000052 and PATO:0002400, or re-typing fusiform as a SKOS concept in a body-shape scheme under a CONVENTIONS section 9 migration, since section 5b rule 5 forbids one IRI being both an OWL class and a SKOS concept. A value set would need two axes, a lateral outline and a cross-section, since FishBase records both. No salmon data source read records body shape, so no term beyond fusiform is being asked for. This choice is separate from the one for smn:alevin (see the body of this card).
gaps.title: Body shape and fusiform

gaps.note: DFO encodes the broodline in its CU identifiers (PKO-nn, PKE-nn) and in the CU life-history-type field, but gcdfo carries no term for it. A term must say that broodline membership individuates the Conservation Unit (DFO splits every pink CU by line) but not the Stock Management Unit: six of DFO's nine pink SMUs contain CUs of both lines.
gaps.title: Broodline

gaps.note: smn PR 27 carries the broodline as the strong reading of hasCycleLine, from a line-individuated unit to its year-series line. That is the right shape, but the wording must be fixed or nearly fixed age and nearly complete closure, not invariant and closed, and the property must not be asserted of a multi-line aggregate. "Broodline" belongs as an alternative label on the two pink line concepts, not on the generic cycle-line concept, because it also names hatchery breeding lines.
gaps.title: Broodline

gaps.note: The draft smn cycle-line scheme excludes dominance, and since the 2026-08-25 revision of PR 27 it names the successor: DFO's three CU fields. Where that successor belongs is open. Dominance statuses are predicated of a population on a line for a period, and the status vocabularies differ by agency (DFO dominant, subdominant, off-year; ADF&G peak, pre-peak, off-cycle; for pink, odd-year dominant, even-year dominant, no dominance), so a shared status scheme would need a crosswalk and DFO's own fields read as agency profile material.
gaps.title: Cyclic dominance

gaps.note: The statistical-modifier scheme has a Count concept defined as a value "counted rather than estimated", and no complement. There is no Estimated modifier, so the very distinction that concept's definition depends on cannot be asserted of the other half of the data. A modifier would have to say that the reported value is inferred from a sample or a model rather than enumerated, and would be the smallest change that implements the shared layer's own ratified policy of carrying estimate semantics as a qualifier rather than as a class.
gaps.title: The estimand and the estimate in salmon assessment

gaps.note: No term is missing here; a relation between two existing terms is. The curated gcdfo-to-smn boundary maps gcdfo:EscapementMeasurement to smn:EscapementEstimate and says nothing at all about gcdfo:SpawnerAbundance, whose own alternate label is "Escapement (count)" and whose definition says it is often operationalized as escapement. So the two layers each carry an escapement-shaped measurement datum and the graph does not relate them. The fix is a mapping row, not a new term — which is why the mint target is do-not-mint — but the row cannot be written until it is settled whether the two denote one quantity or two.
gaps.title: Relating an estimate to its estimand

gaps.note: A female-sex constraint concept for I-ADOPT decomposition: the constraint that a measured population component is female spawners. Searched as "female sex" against smn and gcdfo with no usable candidate. Sex is an all-agency biological axis, so it belongs in the shared layer, and a scheme should anticipate male and unspecified alongside female rather than minting one value. Re-searched 2026-09-26 against smn 0.0.3 and gcdfo 0.0.9: nothing mentions female or sex, and Darwin Core's dwc:sex is a property with no value concepts. PATO_0000383 (female) is an external term the concept could map to. PSC's published stock-recruit data need it for their effective-female-spawner column.
gaps.title: Fraser sockeye stock-recruit decomposition gaps

gaps.note: Smolt and fry life-stage constraint concepts. smn's LifePhaseScheme carries phase/location stratifiers (ocean, terminal, mainstem, in-river), and the PSC CV review recorded smn:LifePhase as rejected_too_broad for exactly smolt/fry — so the need is a developmental life-stage vocabulary (fry, smolt, and siblings such as parr and alevin), distinct from the location-phase axis. Two of the six recipe components land here. Evidence added 2026-09-26: PSC's published data count age-1 and age-2 smolts and count fry either as they migrate down the spawning stream or in the rearing lake, while DFO's glossary confines fry to streams, so the fry concept must be worded to admit lake-rearing sockeye fry. Still absent from smn 0.0.3 and gcdfo 0.0.9. The abundance classes these constraints would qualify are gaps on juvenile-outmigrant-abundance.
gaps.title: Fraser sockeye stock-recruit decomposition gaps

gaps.note: An unspawned-egg adjustment method concept: the procedure that adjusts effective female spawner abundance for egg retention. Searched as "unspawned egg adjustment" with no candidate in either ontology. Methods are SKOS concepts in smn per the S9 methods-as-SKOS ruling, so the mint target is smn's method scheme. Evidence added 2026-09-26: Grant et al. (2011) describe the procedure (spawner success scored as 0, 50 or 100 percent of eggs spawned from carcass surveys; effective female spawners as female spawners times spawner success), and PSC's published documentation describes the same downward adjustment. Still absent from smn 0.0.3 and gcdfo 0.0.9.
gaps.title: Fraser sockeye stock-recruit decomposition gaps

gaps.note: Smolt abundance estimation and fry abundance estimation method concepts — the enumeration procedures behind the recipe's two juvenile abundance series. Searched against both ontologies with no candidate. These sit beside smn's existing enumeration methods and should be minted in the same scheme rather than a new one; whether they are one concept with a life-stage constraint or two concepts is the modelling question a proposal has to answer. PSC's published documentation (2026-09-26) names the juvenile series but not the methods that produced them.
gaps.title: Fraser sockeye stock-recruit decomposition gaps
